description:
## What

Pull DNS rebinding detection out of `CrestHttpClient`.

## Source to move (from `src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr`)

- `verify_dns_rebinding(url)`
- `should_check_dns_rebinding?`
- `extract_host(url)` (URL parsing for host extraction)
- `valid_host?(host)`
- `validate_cached_dns(host, cached)`
- `resolve_and_validate_new_dns(host)`
- `valid_address?(addr)`
- `validate_address_for_host(host, addr)`

## Why

- DNS rebinding is its own concern. It needs: the config flag, the URL
  validator, and the DNSCache. Once `DNSCache` is its own class, this module
  has a clean dep graph.
- The `verify_dns_rebinding` rescue is suspicious: it re-raises `DNSError` but
  swallows everything else with a debug log. That is the kind of thing that
  bites during incidents and should live where the behavior is reviewable.

## API target

    class Fetcher::CrestHttpClient::RebindingChecker
      def initialize(@config : RequestConfig, @validator : URLValidator::Service,
                     @cache : DNSCache)
      def verify(url : String) : Nil
    end

## Constraints

- Behavior must match exactly. In particular, the bare `rescue` that swallows
  non-DNSError exceptions with a debug log stays (it is intentional per the
  comment "DNS rebinding check failed" — rebinding checks should not fail
  the request when DNS is unavailable in some edge environment).
- Must still raise `DNSError` on rebinding detection and on no valid addresses.
- Depends on the DNSCache ticket (uses `cache.get` / `cache.put`).

## Done when

- New file exists.
- `crest_http_client.cr` no longer contains `verify_dns_rebinding` or its
  helpers.
- `crest_http_client_rebinding_spec.cr` and
  `crest_http_client_rebinding_flow_spec.cr` pass unchanged.
title: Extract RebindingChecker into src/fetcher/crest_http_client/rebinding_checker.cr
